discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 221011
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
611 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy fog is expected to continue develop this morning,
  especially south of US Route 24 across northeast Indiana and 
  northwest Ohio. The patchy fog may be locally dense. Fog may 
  become more widespread Thursday night into early Friday 
  morning across northwest Ohio.

- Dry weather and above normal temperatures are expected through the 
  weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 330 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

A short wave trough continues to dive southeast across southeast 
Ontario this morning. Low level ridging is being reinforced behind 
this short wave across the Mid MS River Valley, and this will 
prolong the period of weak gradient that has been in place locally 
the past several days. Ideal radiational cooling conditions this 
morning will continue to support some patchy fog potential, and 
present indications still suggest that southeast portions of the 
area downwind of eastern Great Lakes may experience a brief period 
of greater fog coverage this morning south of US Route 24 across 
northeast Indiana and northwest Ohio. Otherwise for today large 
scale flow amplification is expected as a stronger upper vort lobe 
across southeast Canada phases with an Atlantic vort max. Meanwhile, 
a cut-off upper low will continue to migrate slowly eastward into 
southern California this evening. This evolution will result an 
amplifying low/upper level ridging across central CONUS and south 
central Canada. Low level/near sfc winds will veer more easterly as 
this amplification occurs which will result in continued weak 
thermal advections over the next 24 hours. Thus, a persistence 
forecast has been utilized once again today in terms of max 
temps. The veering low level flow may allow some slightly better
low level moisture to drop south into the area from the Great 
Lakes, but the only possible effect from this weak advection 
would be some very low coverage diurnal cu that will not have 
any impact on temps today.

This transition back to low level easterlies will likely support 
additional stratus/fog development downwind of the eastern Great 
Lakes tonight, with a potential of some dense fog early Friday 
morning across northwest Ohio, south central Michigan, and 
possibly into portions of northeast Indiana. Low temperatures 
tonight will drop back into the low 40s once again, but may dip 
into upper 30s for favored, cool low-lying spots.

Guidance is starting to come into a bit better agreement 
regarding large scale flow through the weekend. A stronger and 
more progressive northern stream upper level system will shift 
across south central Canada this weekend which will drive a cold
front boundary southward across the Great Lakes. Track of this 
northern stream wave is expected to remain well to the north, 
and departure of this wave will likely hang up the front north 
of the local area through the weekend. With forcing/frontal 
position to the north, and narrow zone of better pre-frontal 
moisture transport remaining from the Central Plains to the 
northern Great Lakes, a dry forecast remains intact through 
Monday. The warmest days of this forecast period still look to 
be Sunday/Monday as veered low level flow allows for some modest
increase in low level warm advection.

By Tuesday/Wednesday the southern stream cut-off low is expected to 
eject east and dampen. This wave could interact with the stalled 
frontal boundary across the Upper MS Valley to the Great Lakes with 
some weak isentropic ascent possible. Given dampening nature of this 
wave and likely marginal moisture profiles, blended PoPs remain only 
in the 10 to 20 percent range toward the end of this forecast valid 
period.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 610 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

Fog will continue to be the primary forecast concern through the
period. A west-southwest migration of low level ridge axis has
favored a weak northerly near sfc flow component this morning.
This has kept the bulk of significant fog formation across
northwest Ohio due to Lake Erie influence. Cannot completely 
rule out some brief IFR vsbys in patchy fog early this morning, 
but vertical moisture profiles seems to be more supportive of 
these lower vsbys in NW Ohio. Otherwise, another quiet day in 
store with minimal aviation weather concerns as VFR conditions 
and light winds are expected after any patchy fog dissipates by 
14Z. The amplitude of the low level ridging will increase later 
today into tonight, eventually setting up more of an easterly 
near sfc flow component for tonight into early Friday morning. 
This may be more supportive of greater coverage fog for early 
Friday morning, but early indications would suggest greater risk
just east of KFWA and into NW Ohio.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Marsili
AVIATION...Marsili

spc.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across portions of the Southwest today into tonight, with the most intense cells forecast across parts of Arizona and western New Mexico this afternoon and evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes all appear possible.
spc.text:
SPC AC 221244

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0744 AM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

   Valid 221300Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   CENTRAL/EASTERN ARIZONA INTO WESTERN NEW MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected across portions of the
   Southwest today into tonight, with the most intense cells forecast
   across parts of Arizona and western New Mexico this afternoon and
   evening. Large hail, damaging winds, and a few tornadoes all appear
   possible.

   ...Southwest into the Great Basin...
   Occasional supercells across portions of east-central AZ have
   persisted through much of the early morning hours, aided by
   continued large-scale ascent associated with a 50-70 kt
   south-southwesterly mid-level jet and low-level upslope flow across
   the Mogollon Rim. Strong deep-layer shear of 40-50+ kt and generally
   long/straight hodographs at mid/upper levels noted on the latest
   KFSX/KIWA VWPs will support organized updrafts through the remainder
   of the morning amid 500-1500 J/kg of MUCAPE (greater with southward
   extent). See Mesoscale Discussion 2396 for more details on the
   short-term threat across AZ.

   Current expectations are for additional intense thunderstorms to
   develop by 18-21Z across the higher terrain of east-central AZ and
   vicinity as an upper trough/low over CA moves inland over the Great
   Basin. The mid-level jet attendant to the upper trough/low will also
   translate eastward through the day, with strong deep-layer shear
   remaining over a gradually destabilizing airmass. The primary severe
   threat should remain large hail with any sustained supercells
   (isolated 2+ inches possible). But, the risk for severe/damaging
   winds may increase by mid to late afternoon as convection spreads
   from eastern AZ into western NM, with some potential for clustering.
   A few tornadoes also appear possible, mainly over east-central AZ
   this afternoon when the best combination of greater boundary-layer
   instability and low-level shear are forecast to overlap. While the
   severe threat across these areas will peak in the mid to late
   afternoon when instability is strongest, at least an isolated threat
   should continue through much of the evening with eastward extent
   into western/central NM before convection eventually weakens.

   Farther north into the Great Basin, both low-level moisture and
   related MLCAPE are generally more limited. Even so, multiple
   corridors of isolated severe hail/wind potential may exist this
   afternoon as convection develops ahead of the eastward-translating
   upper trough/low amid strong southerly flow/shear through much of
   the troposphere. Recent short-term guidance suggests a small cluster
   may form and spread northeastward across northern NV into southern
   ID, with some potential for strong to locally severe gusts.

   ...Coastal Southern California...
   Additional organized bands of low-topped convection appear unlikely
   this morning into the afternoon across coastal southern CA.
   Therefore, the Marginal Risk has been removed with this update.

   ..Gleason/Kerr.. 10/22/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1630Z

spc.summary: Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of New Mexico on Friday.
spc.text:
SPC AC 220600

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0100 AM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS PORTIONS OF NEW
   MEXICO...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of New
   Mexico on Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A broad upper trough will slowly progress over the Rockies on
   Friday, with a lead mid-level impulse poised to eject into the
   northern Plains while a lagging 500 mb cut-off low drifts eastward
   across the Desert Southwest. Given adequate low-level moisture
   return and deep-layer ascent ahead of the longwave mid-level trough,
   thunderstorms will be possible across much of the Rockies and the
   central to northern Plains. Isolated severe thunderstorms are
   possible across portions of NM, where locally greater moisture and
   instability reside.

   ...Western into central New Mexico...
   As the aforementioned leading mid-level impulse departs the Rockies
   and the cut-off low approaches NM, 50+ kt southwesterly 500 mb flow
   will overspread the Desert Southwest, where low to mid 50s F surface
   dewpoints amid southeasterly surface flow will be in place. Given
   7-7.5 C/km mid-level lapse rates, up to 1000 J/kg MLCAPE may
   manifest amid appreciably curved and elongated hodographs, with
   30-40 kts of effective bulk shear likely. By afternoon,
   thunderstorms should develop and intensify with diurnal heating.
   Given the aforementioned vertical shear/buoyancy, some supercell
   structures should develop, accompanied by an isolated severe
   wind/hail threat, and a tornado is also possible.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/22/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 220718

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0218 AM CDT Thu Oct 22 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR CENTRAL NEW
   MEXICO INTO FAR WEST TEXAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe wind/hail or a tornado are possible across portions
   of central New Mexico into Far West Texas on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid-level cut-off low will traverse the Desert Southwest and
   impinge on the southern High Plains on Saturday. This will provoke a
   low-level mass response in the form of northwestward moisture
   advection through the day. Cooler temperatures and stronger flow
   aloft associated with the cut-off low will overspread the low-level
   moisture, resulting in enough buoyancy and shear overlap to support
   an isolated severe threat.

   ...Portions of central NM into Far West TX...
   Through the afternoon, 40-50 kt south-southwesterly mid-level flow
   and 7+ C/km mid-level lapse rates from the approaching cut-off low
   will overspread mid to upper 50s F surface dewpoints and backed
   southeasterly surface winds. With surface heating of the
   aforementioned moist low-level airmass, MLCAPE may exceed 1000 J/kg,
   perhaps locally exceeding 1500 J/kg in spots given locally greater
   insolation. Veering and strengthening flow with height will yield
   modestly curved and elongated hodographs, with over 40 kts of
   effective bulk shear expected. Multicells and perhaps a couple of
   supercells may develop and persist for at least a few hours before
   merging into a loosely organized line of thunderstorms. Storms
   should be at their strongest during their supercell stage, capable
   of producing isolated severe hail/wind and perhaps a tornado.

   ..Squitieri.. 10/22/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
